You can create devastating fields of antigravity.

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Antigravity
Starting at 1st level, you have learned how to use your technique to manipulate gravity, allowing you to make a small gravitational field around yourself. As an action for 3 cursed energy, you can reverse gravity in a 10 foot-radius 30 foot-high cylinder centered on you for all creatures but yourself until the beginning of your next turn.

All creatures and objects that aren’t anchored to the ground in the area fall upward. A creature can make a Dexterity saving throw to grab onto a fixed object it can reach, thus avoiding the fall. If a solid object (such as a ceiling) is encountered in this fall, falling objects and creatures strike it and take the remaining height as fall damage. If an object or creature reaches the top of the area without striking anything, it remains there, oscillating slightly, for the duration. At the end of the duration, affected objects and creatures fall back down, taking fall damage.

The height of the cylinder increases to 50 feet at 3rd level, 100 feet at 11th level and 200 feet at 18th level. Fall damage from this technique ignores any type of fall damage reduction or immunity. Fall damage die becomes d8 at 3rd level and d10 at 6th level.

Gravity Field
At 3rd level, you gained the following benefits through practicing your technique.
Light Fall. As a reaction for 1 CE to falling, you and creatures equal to your proficiency bonus within 120 feet have their rate of descent slowed to 60 feet per round and take no fall damage when you land.
Focused System. When you use your innate technique, you can choose a number of creatures equal to your CE modifier + your proficiency bonus to be unaffected by your technique.
Disorienting Gravity. Any creature that is lifted upwards by your Antigravity must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, they make any attacks at disadvantage and cannot maintain concentration while within your field.

Antigravity Shield
At 6th level, you have learned to defend yourself from attacks using your antigravity. As a reaction for 2 CE, you can encase yourself in a field of antigravity, causing attack rolls against you to be made at disadvantage and any damage other than psychic is reduced by your CE modifier + your level until the beginning of your next turn. If you are taking the Dodge action, you can use this reaction on another creature within 5 feet.

Boosted System
At 11th level, you master all aspects of your technique and gain the following improvements to your Antigravity:
Lasting Field. You can spend additional CE up to your modifier to increase the range by 10 feet and the duration by 1 round per CE.
Sweeping Gravity. Creatures with a Dexterity score below your CE save DC cannot make a Dexterity saving throw against your technique.
Nauseating Gravity. If a creature fails a saving throw against your Disorienting Gravity, they are also stunned until the end of their next turn.
Hard Fall. Fall damage from your field becomes d12 bludgeoning.

Domain Expansion: Zero Gravity
At 18th level you have learned how to expand your domain. At initiative 20, all creatures of your choice are affected by and fail all saving throws against Antigravity, which can be released by you at will.

By covering your face you can become a medium for the spirit of the four auspicious beasts. These four beasts give you great abilities.

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.
You regain all spent cursed energy on a long rest.

Auspicious Beast #1: Kaichi
Beginning at 1st level, as an action using 1 Cursed Energy, you summon a yellow drill horn for 1 minute. This horn can be used to make an additional melee Cursed Energy attack against a creature within 30 ft as part of your turn, dealing 1d6 piercing damage on a hit. The damage increases to 1d8 at 3rd level, 1d10 at 6th level, 1d12 at 11th level, and 3d6 at 18th level. You can only have one Kaichi at a time.

Auspicious Beast #2: Reiki
At 3rd level, you summon dark water to assist yourself. You can use a bonus action to spend 1 Cursed Energy and double your movement until the end of your next turn. Additionally, as a reaction for 2 Cursed Energy, you gain a +5 bonus to AC until the beginning of your next turn.

Auspicious Beast #3: Kirin
Once you reach 6th level, you gain a power to help you last longer in battles. As a bonus action, for every 1 Cursed Energy you spend you gain 5 temporary hit points.
While you have these temporary hit points, you ignore exhaustion. However, after activating, your movement is 0 until the start of your next turn.

Auspicious Beast #4: Ryu
When you get to 11th level, you gain the last and most powerful Auspicious Beast. As an action for 10 Cursed Energy, you unleash the full power of a dragon. When you use this action, you summon Ryu within 30 ft of you. A creature where Ryu is summoned must make a Strength saving throw or take 8d10 piercing damage. Ryu lasts for up to 10 minutes or until you are unconscious and you can command Ryu as a bonus action. Otherwise Ryu takes the dodge action and defends itself. You can summon one Ryu at a time. Once destroyed, you cannot summon Ryu again for 10 minutes.

Domain Expansion: Auspicious Beasts’ Realm
Finally, at 18th level, you have honed your Cursed Technique to an extreme. While in this domain, all of your Auspicious Beasts are constantly active without side effects. Attacks made by Kaichi and Ryu always hit. Kirin refreshes at initiative 20 as if you spent Cursed Energy up to your CE modifier.

You were born with a simple ability many called weak, the ability to control and see through crows.

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.
You regain all spent cursed energy on a long rest.

Cursed Crows
At 1st level, you have learned how to imbue crows with cursed energy to use them as part of your technique. As an action for 1 Cursed Energy, you can imbue a raven with cursed energy if it's restrained, grappled, or incapacitated. It then becomes one of your cursed crows, it will become charmed by you and will follow your orders. As an action, you can close your eyes giving you the blinded condition unless you have blindsight, while you see through one of your crows. While seeing through your crows, you can use your passive Perception instead of the crows. You can only see through one crow at a time and can switch between them as an action or stop as a bonus action. You start with 3 cursed crows.

Omen of Death
When you reach 3rd level, you are constantly followed by an omen of death, giving you an aura of terror. As a bonus action, you force each creature of your choice that you can see within 30 ft to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, a creature becomes frightened of you for 1 minute. A frightened creature can repeat the save at the end of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
You have advantage on attack rolls against frightened creatures.
Raven’s Eye
Starting at 6th level, your crows have been enhancing your sight. You will gain +1 to your passive perception for every crow you currently have. In addition, you can switch between crows as a bonus action and can stop seeing through them at will.

Bird Strike
Beginning 11th level, your mastery of Black Bird Manipulation has made you develop its most powerful technique. As an action for 8 Cursed Energy, you can order one of your crows to launch themselves at a creature from their flying speed range. The target must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they take 10d10 necrotic damage and have one of their limbs damaged, rolling a d6 to see the damaged limb. On a successful save, they take half as much damage and do not have a limb damaged. The crow dies afterwards.

Domain Expansion: Black Mahakala
If you reach 18th level, you gain your domain expansion. At Initiative 20, you can choose up to three targets to suffer the full effects of Bird Strike for no cost. The crows still die afterwards.

You can create incredibly tough black cube barriers.

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Dark Cube
Starting at 1st level, you can spend 2 cursed energy as an action to create an immovable 10 feet opaque black cube within 30 feet of you for 1 minute or until you end it as a free action. If a Large or smaller creature is within range, they must make a Dexterity saving throw or be trapped within the cube. A creature inside your cube has full cover against attacks outside the cube and creatures other than you are blinded if there isn’t a source of light inside the cube.
The cube has an AC equal to your Cursed Energy save DC + 5, hit points equal to your proficiency bonus times twice your Cursed Energy modifier and immunity to psychic and poison damage.

Black Box Reinforcement
Starting at 3rd level you can reinforce your barriers with cursed energy. You can spend additional cursed energy up to your Cursed Energy modifier to give your Dark Cube a reinforcement for every cursed energy spent:
Persistence. Your Cube gains 10 additional hit points for every 1 reinforcement, +1 bonus to AC for every 2 reinforcements and lasts an additional minute for every 3 reinforcements.
Toughness. Your Cube reduces all damage taken by 1 for each reinforcement.
Size. For every 2 reinforcements, you can make your Dark Cube 5 feet larger, allowing you to fit more creatures. (10 ft < 15 ft < 20ft)
At 11th level, you can spend up to twice your CE modifier on reinforcements.

Perfect Cube
At 6th level, you have learned to create a nearly indestructible Dark Cube. For an additional 5 CE, you can create a Perfect Cube (this cursed energy counts towards the Cube’s Reinforcements).
Your Perfect Cube has resistance to all damage and ignores features or abilities that deal higher damage against objects and structures or would destroy, see into, or invade your barrier.

Maximum: Midnight Armor
At 11th level, you have learned to manifest your barrier around yourself. You can spend 6 cursed energy as an action to manifest parts of your cube around your body like armor for 1 minute or until the armor is destroyed:

  • You gain the hit points of your barrier as temporary hit points.

  • Your AC equals your Dark Cube’s AC.

  • Your unarmed strikes can use your CE modifier for attack rolls and deal 3d8 + CE modifier necrotic damage on a hit.

  • You can spend additional cursed energy up to twice your cursed energy modifier to also gain the benefits of any reinforcement other than Size.

Domain Expansion: Primordial Gap
At 18th level you have mastered your technique, allowing you to expand your domain. In your domain all of your Dark Cubes automatically count as Perfect Cubes. At initiative 20, you create 3 Perfect Cubes, potentially trapping 3 creatures within your domain inside Perfect Cubes. They are treated as having Reinforcements up to your CE modifier. These cubes disappear when your domain ends.

Through your beliefs, you set both your weapon and heart alight with your blazing courage.

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Ignition
Starting at 1st level, your technique allows yourself to ignite your weapon in flames, increasing your fire power. You can spend up to your proficiency bonus as a bonus action while holding a melee weapon, igniting said weapon in flames for 1 minute. For the duration, the weapon deals an additional 1d6 fire damage on a hit per CE spent, and emits bright light for 5 feet and dim light for another 10 feet.
This increases to 1d8 per ce spent at 6th level and again to 1d10 at 11th level and 1d12 at 18th level.

                     **Mantle of Courage**

Starting at 3rd level, you can strengthen both yourself and your weapon. When you use Ignition, you ignore any detriments or penalties of the weapon or can use it on yourself for your unarmed strikes, potentially recreating a lost limb for the duration.
While Ignition is active, you can spend 3 CE as a free action on your turn. You emit an aura of flames within 10 feet of you for 1 minute, giving you resistance to fire and cold damage. An enemy that enters your mantle or starts their turn there must make a Constitution saving throw, taking your Ignition damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful save.
Eternal Flames
At 6th level, when you spend at least 3 ce on Ignition, you can increase the weapon’s range by 10 feet, ignore resistance to fire damage and when you miss with a weapon attack by 2 or less, you deal half your Ignition damage.
This increases to 3 or less at 11th level and 4 or less at 18th level.

Maximum: Conflagration
At 11th level, while your technique may be simple, that does not mean it isn’t powerful. While holding a melee weapon you can spend 10 ce as an action to swing your weapon, creating a 30 feet cone of intense flame and heat. All creatures within range must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 10d12 fire damage and being knocked prone on a failed save or half as much on a successful save.
If a creature fails by 5 or more, they gain severe burns and take additional fire damage equal to your proficiency bonus from any source of fire damage until they finish a long rest.

Domain Expansion: Fire of the Heart
Finally at 18th level you have learned to expand your domain. Any melee weapon you are holding is treated as having the maximum cursed energy used for Ignition and is imbued with your domain’s guaranteed hit. At initiative 20, all creatures of your choice within your domain suffer the damage of your Mantle of Courage.

You were born with a complex ability held and practiced by the Kamo family, you can control your blood.

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.
You regain all spent cursed energy on a long rest.

Blood Constructs
Starting at 1st level, you have been blessed with the Innate Technique of the Kamo clan, making you begin with the most basic technique, the blood constructs. You can pull blood from an available source to create a semi-solid construct. As an action for 1 CE and 1 HP, you can create a small construct smaller than a 5ft by 5ft space. For every 5 ft the price increases by 1 CE and HP. You can ignore the HP cost if you have an alternate source of blood. These constructs have HP equal to your level times CE spent.
Once as part of a long rest, you can spend $100 and hit points up to your proficiency bonus to fill a Blood Bag with your own blood. This Blood Bag counts as a source of hit points for your Blood Manipulation features. A Blood Bag lasts 5 days outside of refrigeration before it goes bad. You can have a number of Blood Bags equal to your Constitution modifier at once.

Blood Techniques
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your blood in a manner fit for battle. When you use a Blood Manipulation feature, you can ignore the HP cost if you have an alternate source of blood. You gain three of following techniques and gain an additional two at 6th and 11th level:

  • Crimson Binding: As an action for 1 CE and 1 HP, you unleash a red blood net, forcing a target Large or smaller within 30ft to make a Strength saving throw or be restrained. They can repeat the save at the start of their turn.

  • Slicing Exorcism: As an action for 1 CE and 1 HP you spin a ring of blood and unleash it as a projectile. Make a ranged CE attack against a target within 60 ft, on a hit you deal 1d10 + CE modifier necrotic damage. If used with Convergence, the attack still deals your CE modifier on a miss of 5 or less.

  • Blood Edge: You can spend CE up to your Cursed Energy modifier to create a melee weapon as a free action which counts as magical for overcoming resistances. For every two Cursed Energy used the weapon gains an additional damage tier(d10->d12->2d8) and lasts 1 minute. If used with Convergence, it only gains the benefit of the damage tier increase.

  • Crimson Rain: As an action for 3 CE and 2 HP, you pick an area within 60 ft, that spot becomes the center of a 15 ft radius of a rain of blood spikes. All creatures in that radius must make a Dexterity Saving throw taking 3d10 piercing damage on failure or half as much on a success. If used with Convergence, a target is also knocked prone on a failed save.

  • Blood Burst: For 1 CE and 1 HP upon hitting with a weapon attack once per turn, you cover your strike with blood, causing it to explode on impact. The creature must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure they take 4d6 necrotic damage.

  • Blood Meteorite: As an action for 1 CE and 3 HP you create a solid crystal of blood launched like an asteroid. You can make a ranged CE attack against a target in 30 ft. On a hit, this attack deals 4d4 + CE modifier in bludgeoning damage.

  • Blood Geyser: As an action for 3 CE and 3 HP, you can choose a 5 feet space within 10 ft of yourself and saturate it with blood. When a creature starts their turn there or enters that area, all creatures within 5 feet must make a Dexterity saving throw or take 5d10 bludgeoning damage and get launched 30ft in the air or half as much on a success.

Flowing Red Scale
At 3rd level, you can control body temperature, pulse rate, and the number of red blood cells to give yourself greatly increased physical capabilities. You can spend 3 Cursed Energy as a bonus action to gain the following benefits for 1 minute:

  • Your walking speed is doubled

  • You gain a +2 bonus to your AC

  • You advantage on Dexterity saving throws and Strength checks

  • You gain an additional action on each of your turns. That action can be used only to take the Attack (one weapon attack only), Dash, Disengage, Hide, or Use an Object action.

Convergence
At 6th level, you compress and condense blood to its absolute limit. Before you use a blood manipulation technique with a casting time of one action, you can spend your bonus action, reaction and movement to enhance the technique's potency, gaining the following benefits:

  • You deal additional damage die equal to your proficiency bonus

  • Your damage die increases by 1 level(d10->d12->2d8)

  • The range increases by 30 feet

If you spend an additional turn using your action, bonus action, reaction and movement to charge up Convergence before using your technique, you gain these benefits an additional time and gain advantage on the first technique attack roll or can force creatures to make their first saving throw against your technique at disadvantage. Certain Blood Techniques may have additional or different bonuses if used with Convergence that are listed with each technique.

Alternatively, instead of spending time to compress blood, you quicken the process with cursed energy. You can spend 1 additional CE when using a Blood Technique to gain additional benefits. Slicing Exorcism, Blood Burst and Blood Meteorite deal 1 additional damage dice on a hit. Crimson Binding increases the DC by 1. Crimson Rain and Blood Geyser deal 1 additional damage per damage dice.
At 11th level, the additional CE you can spend increases to 2, which causes these bonuses to double if spending 2 instead of 1. At 18th level, this becomes 3 CE, which can cause these bonuses to triple. You cannot use both methods of Convergence on the same technique.

Piercing Blood
Beginning at 11th level, you can compress your blood into a deadly supersonic beam. As an action for 8 CE and 5 HP, you unleash a 100ft line of blood. Creatures in range must make a Dexterity save taking 10d8 piercing on a failure.
If used with Convergence, you can continue shooting the beam for an additional round. Any creature that enters the lingering Piercing Blood must make the saving throw. As an action you can swing the line, making it into a 130 feet cone forcing an additional Dexterity save and the technique ends.

Domain Expansion: Bloodbath
When you reach 18th level, you gain your domain expansion. At Initiative 20, all creatures take 4d12 necrotic damage as their blood attacks them from the inside. While in the domain your blood manipulation techniques can use hit points from other creatures within the domain.

You were born with a simple although tricky ability to swap places with your opponents with a clap.

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.
You regain all spent cursed energy on a long rest.

Boogie
At 1st level, you have created a unique technique to switch places with your others, extremely simple yet effective. You can switch places with a willing creature or magical object within 30 feet of you by clapping for 1 Cursed Energy. You can use this technique as an action or bonus action, or you can also swap as a reaction for 2 additional Cursed Energy.

Woogie
Starting at 3rd level, you have extended the grasp of your technique as well as its versatility. Your Boogie gains the following bonuses:

  • Unwilling creatures can be switched

  • You can make two creatures other than yourself swap places

  • Enemies teleported are disorientated and lose their reaction

Clap Back
Beginning at 6th level, “The act of applause is an acclamation of the soul”, you have gained a deeper understanding of your technique and how it can be used, your Boogie gains the following benefits:

  • Your range increases to 45 feet.

  • The Cursed Energy cost is reduced by 1 Cursed Energy for all Boogie Woogie techniques (min cost of 1).

  • You can use Boogie once per turn as a free action for 1 cursed energy.

Round of Applause
When you reach 11th level, you have understood the true depths of Boogie Woogie, your Boogie gains the following:

  • Your range increases to 60 feet

  • When you switch places with an ally who was previously in melee range of an enemy right before the switch, your next attack roll has advantage, the same goes if you teleport an enemy into range or an ally into range.

  • You can use Boogie on up to four creatures at once.

Domain Expansion: Standing Ovation
Reaching 18th level, you have mastered the beat of Boogie Woogie, you gain your domain expansion. Within your domain, you can use Boogie as a free action an unlimited number of times on your turn (not limited to once per turn) without spending CE.

You were born with the horrifying but useful ability to swap bodies and take the abilities from that body.

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.
You regain all spent cursed energy on a long rest.

Graverobber
Starting at 1st level, you have a rather disgusting technique, which is frowned upon by the majority of sorcerers. When you have a humanoid creature's corpse, you can spend 1 cursed energy during a long rest to put your brain on that creature through a transfer technique. While on the creature's body, you lose any racial features of your old body but keep all of your class features. You gain the following benefits while inside the body:

  • The creature’s innate technique features are now yours.

  • The creature’s cursed energy features are now yours.

  • The creature's racial features are now yours.

  • The creature's ability scores overwrite yours but you keep your Charisma, Wisdom, and Intelligence scores.

  • The creature's proficiencies and languages are now yours.

When you change into that creature's body, it will look the same outside of having a scar on its forehead, which is a sign your brain is inside its body. You can pull the top of your head to show your brain, which is a normal brain with a human mouth. Other creatures can try to identify you're not the humanoid by making a DC 30 Insight check. Creatures who knew the body's owner before you stole it can do the roll with advantage.
Skill Theft
Beginning at 3rd, your control over the body you take over increases. You can choose to take two of the body’s Innate Technique features. Cursed Energy features, or proficiencies from a body you have inhabited in the past. You cannot use Innate Technique features from different techniques at the same time. If you do, one of them deactivates until you are only using one innate technique. You can choose two more features at 6th, 11th, and 18th levels.

Immortality
At the 18th level, your age is the same as the body you take over, making you immortal as long as you keep switching bodies.

Your technique summons a centipede shikigami to fight with you.

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Cursed Centipede
Starting at 1st level, you can summon your shikigami as a bonus action. You can command your shikigami on your turn as a bonus action. Your centipede can enter your space, floating around you as a shroud providing the following benefits:

  • On a hit with a melee attack, you deal an additional 1d10 damage as your Centipede fights with you.

  • You gain a bonus to AC equal to your proficiency bonus.

  • You can make an additional melee attack as a bonus action.

  • When you or the centipede take damage, you can choose to have the other take the damage instead. If this damage would reduce the centipede to 0 hit points, you take the remaining damage.

You can summon your shikigami for free once per long rest and again for 3 CE. You can only have one Cursed Centipede summoned at a time. The centipede cannot be targeted with attacks directly while acting as a Shroud. However, if you are reduced to 0 HP, any remaining damage affects the shikigami.

Insect Storage
Starting at 3rd level, you can store items in the stomach of your centipede. You must have your centipede summoned to take items in or out of it and items can be no larger than a shield or polearm. Your centipede can store a number of pounds equal to twice your Cursed Energy score times your proficiency bonus and you can store or withdraw an item as an object interaction. If you die, the items stored in your centipede explode from your stomach.
Earthquake
Starting at 6th level, as an action you can spend 3 CE to force all creatures within 30 feet to make a Strength saving throw if they are on the ground. On a failure, they take 6d6 bludgeoning damage and fall prone. On a success, they take half as much damage. If your cursed centipede is summoned, you can instead do this as a bonus action. This damage increases to 10d6 at 11th and 14d6 at 18th level.

Additionally, you gain 5 stat points you can spend to increase your centipede’s ability scores (max of 22). You can now add your proficiency bonus to any saving throw or skill check it makes.
You gain 5 additional stat points at 11th level.

Hundred Leg Catastrophe
At 11th level, your technique increases by leaps and bounds. As an action for 8 cursed energy, you can launch up to 3 giant centipedes at targets within 120 feet, making a ranged cursed energy attack roll for each. On a hit, they deal 8d10 necrotic damage and the target must make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, the target is pushed or pulled 30ft closer or further (your choice) and falls prone.
Additionally, you can now have two cursed centipedes summoned at a time. While you have two cursed centipedes acting as your shroud, you can make 2 melee attacks as a bonus action and instead add 3 + your proficiency bonus to your AC.

Domain Expansion: Oomukade Banzai
At 18th level, you have mastered your technique allowing you to open your domain. Within your domain, your cursed centipedes’s attacks are guaranteed hits. At initiative 20, all creatures are restrained by cursed centipedes and can make a Strength (Athletics) check at the beginning of their turns to escape. The centipedes restraining a creature assists all attacks against the target, causing such attacks to deal an additional 2d10 damage. The cursed centipedes disappear once the domain ends or the creature is no longer grappled.

Your technique allows you to create perfect clones of yourself.

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

One Man Army
Starting at 1st level, you can spend 3 CE as an action to create a clone within 5 feet of yourself for 8 hours. They are completely indistinguishable from you in every way. A clone has 1/4 of your hit point maximum (rounded up) as well as your AC and access to all your class features and cursed techniques, but not innate technique features. Any cursed energy or features used is treated as if you spent it. Your Clones act on your turn, but can only make one attack on their turn even if you have Extra Attack or bonus action attacks. You can replace any of your attacks on your turn with an attack from the Clone’s space. Your Clones do not have any of your items.
You can have a number of clones equal to your proficiency bonus at once and when a clone dies, the number of clones you can have is reduced by 1 for 1 minute.

Twice the Fun
At 3rd level, you can now create multiple clones as an action by spending 3 CE for each clone. When you make a melee attack against a creature while a Clone is within 5 feet of the target, you gain advantage on the attack roll.

Three is a Crowd
At 6th level you have become more skillful and efficient with the creation of your clones. Your Clones now have 1/2 of your total hit points. When one of your Clones is reduced to 0 hit points, you regain 1 cursed energy.

Four is a Party
At 11th level, you have mastered the ability to choose which of your Clones is your actual body. Your Clones have hit points equal to yours and you can swap bodies with one of your clones as a bonus action for 1 CE, trading hit points and causing that Clone to become your new body. When you are reduced to 0 hit points or killed outright while you have a Clone active, you can instead transfer yourself into one of your clones, gaining the Clone’s current hit points.

Your Clones can now create one Clone by spending your Cursed Energy with each Clone counting against your limit.

Domain Expansion: Divide and Conquer
Finally at 18th level you have perfected your technique, allowing you to expand your domain. You can now create one Clone as a bonus action without spending cursed energy once per turn (Your Clones do not gain this benefit). Within your domain, you can have an unlimited number of Clones. Your Clone’s attacks are guaranteed hits within your domain.
At initiative 20, an additional clone appears. All Clones created with your domain disappear when the domain ends.

Why do you need an explanation? How about a joke!

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Comedy

Starting at 1st level, you gain the ability to invert the damage you take. As a bonus action, you can spend 2 cursed energy to activate Inverse for 1 minute. While Inverse is active, when you take damage, it is modified based on a damage limit and threshold. The damage limit equals your proficiency bonus times your Cursed Energy score, and the threshold is equal to your proficiency bonus times your Cursed Energy modifier.
When you take damage that exceeds your threshold, you subtract the threshold from the damage and take the remaining difference as damage. However, when the damage is below your threshold, you subtract the threshold from the damage and take the resulting number as damage instead. For example, if your set limit is 100 and you take 90 damage, you would subtract the damage from your limit if it exceeds the threshold (e.g., 90 - 20 = 70), and take the remaining 70 damage. Conversely, if the damage is below the threshold (e.g., 10 damage), you subtract that amount from your set limit (100 - 10 = 90), and take 90 damage instead. If the calculation results in a negative number, the damage remains unchanged.
You can extend the duration of Inverse by spending 1 cursed energy to maintain the effect for an additional minute.

For example, if your threshold is 15 and you take 10 damage, you treat that as vulnerability. But if you take 18 damage, you instead halve it due to your resistance, even if that type of damage would normally ignore resistances.

★Imai, ★Acrux, ★Mimosa, ★Ginan and ★Gacrux.

Size Damage Dice
Tiny 1d4
Small d6
Medium d8

The order of the stars is as follows: ★Imai → ★Acrux → ★Mimosa → ★Ginan → ★Gacrux

Totality
Any shikigami reduced to 0 hit points dies and cannot be summoned again. A destroyed shikigami is eligible for Totality, with the exception of Rabbit Escape or Mahoraga.

When you make a Totality, they gain the following changes:

  • Their Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Wisdom, and Charisma scores become those of the creature who has the higher score. Then they gain a bonus to that ability score equal to the modifier of the creature with the smaller score.(Ex: Nue has 16 Strength while Divine Dog has 12, their Totality would have 17 Strength.) They also gain the higher AC of the shikigami used.

  • They receive the hit points of both creatures.

  • Their movement speed is added together.(2 with 30 would have 60)

  • They receive all features, traits, actions, bonus actions, reactions, legendary actions, skill, saving throw proficiencies, damage resistances, damage immunities and condition immunities from both creatures.

  • Their size can be either of the shikigami.

  • The CE cost becomes the higher shikigami + half of the lower shikigami’s cost.

  • Their CR equals the creature with a higher CR + half the CR of the creature with the smaller CR rounded up.(Ex: Nue's CR is 4, and Great Serpent's CR is 5, their totality's CR would be 7)

  • After calculating ability scores, the difference in the ability modifier of the original user of a damaging feature and the Totality is added to the amount of dice. For save effects damage, the score corresponding to the save is used.
    (Ex: Mourn Tiger has a +5 in Dexterity and Nue has a +3. Mourn Tiger’s Dexterity Score increases by +3, meaning a +1 bonus to Dexterity modifier so you add 1 additional dice to the Totality's attack to the damage dice that use Dexterity as the ability modifier, changing Mourn Tiger’s bite attack from a 1d10+5 into a 2d10+6.) -Cursed Technique = User’s Cursed Energy save DC + 2
You cannot copy Domain Expansions or CR 5+ Summons with Mimicry.
When you copy a cursed technique, you can only spend the base cost the technique requires. No matter what you copy, you can only use the technique in its base form. For example, a maximum output hollow purple would only come as a hollow purple. You cannot use different copied techniques at the same time if they are from different innate techniques.
You can have a number of copied techniques features equal to your Cursed Energy Modifier and can use them a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus before they disappear and you must copy them again. If you have a limb or body part of the user, the number of times you can use the technique is doubled. When you copy more than your limit, you remove a copied feature to make space for another.
In addition, you automatically pass the Cursed Energy check if you have already copied the cursed technique before.

Stronger Bond
Once you reach 11th level, the bond between the binding object and the Vengeful Spirit becomes stronger. Your Vengeful Spirit gains the following benefits:

  • Two of its ability scores will be increased by 2, and so will their maximum.

  • You will gain +2 to your CE score, including its maximum while your spirit is summoned.

  • Whenever it is summoned the Vengeful Spirit will gain temporary hit points equal to half your current hit points.

Domain Expansion: True Mutual Love
Finally at 18th level, through many battles and copies, you have learned how to expand your domain. Inside this barrier, you are allowed to use all of the cursed techniques you currently have for no Cursed Energy. At initiative 20, you will also gain one additional action, which can only be used to activate a copied cursed technique, which affects all hostile creatures inside the barrier.

You get stronger by eating.

Cursed Energy
Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Hunger of the Accursed
Starting at 1st level, you are constantly filled with the hunger impulses that come with your technique. When you reduce a cursed spirit, shikigami, or cursed corpse to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to spend 3 cursed energy to devour its corpse. For 1 hour you gain a feature, action, movement, resistance, immunity, sense, AC, Ability Score or other statistic from the dead creature’s statblock such as Cursed Energy Affinity (Cannot take legendary actions, Cursed Energy or Domains). You can spend an additional 3 cursed energy to steal an additional ability and can steal a number of abilities from a single corpse up to your Cursed Energy modifier.
When you steal an ability that does not suit your body (such as fly speed), your body changes to fit the ability (eg. growing wings). For the duration, you count as the creature type your stolen abilities come from. If you have stolen abilities from multiple creatures, you count as the one you have the most abilities from. You can have stolen abilities equal to your Cursed Energy modifier active at once.
At 6th level, you can have stolen abilities from a number of creatures equal to your Cursed Energy modifier +2 active at once and last for 24 hours. You cannot use different innate techniques at once.

Regurgitation
At 3rd level, you have learned to access previous abilities you have eaten. As a bonus action you can spend 4 cursed energy to gain an ability you have stolen in the past and can use it for 1 hour. This does not increase at 6th level.
Digestion
At 6th level, your stomach calls for satiation and gives you the means to feed it. The amount of cursed energy required for Hunger of the Accursed and Regurgitation decreases by 1 (minimum cost of 1).

Additionally, you have learned to use cursed energy to enhance the abilities of the devoured. You can use one of the following benefits once per turn when you use a stolen ability:
Efficiency. When you use an ability with a base cursed energy cost, the cost of the feature decreases by 1 (minimum cost of 1).
Output. When you use an ability that lets you spend up to a certain amount of cursed energy, you can increase that amount by 2.
Speed. When using stolen movement, you can spend up to your proficiency bonus to increase it by 5 ft per cursed energy spent.
Reinforcement. When using stolen AC and are hit by an attack roll, you can spend 1 CE to add your proficiency bonus to your AC against that attack roll, potentially causing it to miss.
Instinct. When using a feature, you can spend 2 cursed energy to decrease its action cost by one (Full-Turn Action > Action > Bonus Action > Reaction).

Maximum: Body of the Devourer
At 11th level you have learned to draw the power of the devoured from your stomach and into your flesh. As an action you can transform into one of the creatures you have devoured, spending cursed energy equal to twice the Devoured’s CR (min of 1) or Level. Your statistics are replaced by the statblock of the chosen Devoured, but you retain your alignment, personality, mental scores, Cursed Energy and Hit Points.
You gain temporary hit points equal to the Hit Points of the Devoured. These Temporary Hit Points vanish if any remain when the technique ends. The technique ends early if you have no Temporary Hit Points from this technique left.

You are limited in the actions it can perform by the anatomy of your new form and can only use your cursed techniques if your new form is capable of forming hand signs and chanting. This form lasts for a number of minutes equal to your level + your cursed energy modifier. You cannot use or benefit from Regurgitation while using this feature.

Domain Expansion: Tomb of the Devoured
At 18th level you have mastered your technique allowing you to expand your domain. At initiative 20, you can regurgitate a creature whose corpse you devoured into an unoccupied space within 5 ft of you. The creature is friendly to you and your allies and acts immediately after your turn, attacking all enemies within your domain whether you command it to or not. If the creature was sentient in life, it is barely sentient within your domain as a mere husk of its former self. All regurgitated creatures disappear once your domain ends.
